lead: The right Segway or e-scooter tour is the one that fits your day: a first 90-minute ride past Parliament with your own guide (that is the #1 pick, €45), a 2-hour loop that rolls up to Fisherman's Bastion, a wide-wheel e-scooter that covers more ground, or an evening ride when the riverside is quieter. If you would rather pedal, the bike and e-bike tours have their own comparison. This page gets you to that ride in under a minute.

To make the choice easy, I compared all 9 on what really decides it: whether the route climbs Castle Hill, ride time and price per hour, private or shared group, age and weight limits, and what costs extra, checked on each seller's own page. Filter by Segway, e-scooter, Castle Hill, private or kids below, or scroll straight to the ranking.

review: This is the safest first booking. For €45 you get 90 minutes on a Segway with your own guide, starting with a 15-minute training session at the Galamb utca shop, then a flat Pest loop: Erzsébet Square, St Stephen's Basilica, Liberty Square, Parliament and the Shoes on the Danube Bank, with the castle and Fisherman's Bastion in view across the river.

Compared with its neighbours it trades distance for comfort. The 1-hour Express (#5) costs €10 less but is shorter and shared, while the Buda and Pest loops (#2, #4) add the climb to Castle Hill for about €10 more. What #1 adds is the private format and photos taken for you, which is why it suits nervous first-timers, couples and families with kids from 8.
The catch is the map: it stays on the Pest side. If the view from Fisherman's Bastion is the point of your ride, pick #2 or #4 instead.

guide.h2: Segway, MonsteRoller or EZRaider: Which Is Easiest?
guide.html:
Segway: the easiest to learn. Every Segway tour here starts with 10–15 minutes of training, and you lean to move. The catch is the weight window (most cap riders at 125–140 kg and need 29–30 kg minimum) and the need to step on and off unaided.

MonsteRoller wide-wheel e-scooter (#3, #9): faster (up to 25 km/h) and closer to riding a bike. No licence is needed, but the operator recommends bike or scooter experience, drivers must be 14+, and the guided tour gives no refund if you cannot ride after practice.

EZRaider (#8): four wheels and hand controls make it the most stable, and the only one that takes small children (in tandem from 3).

Prefer to pedal? Compare the Budapest bike and e-bike tours; for the Castle District on foot, see the Buda Castle tours.

• First time on a Segway, want it easy: #1, the 90-minute private ride (€45).
  • Want Fisherman's Bastion and Parliament in one go: #2 (€54), or #4 if you want it private or guided in another language.
  • Group of friends who ride bikes: #3 MonsteRoller, then pick the route length.
  • Only an hour free: #5 Express (€35).
  • Want the full city in one ride: #6, 3 hours with Margaret Island.
  • Evening plans: #7 night ride, then a night cruise.
  • Kids under 6: #8 EZRaider.
  • No guide, lowest price: #9 rental.

guide.h2: Before You Ride: Meeting Points, What to Bring, What Costs Extra
guide.html:
Meeting points: seven of the nine start in District V (postcode 1052): GetSegway at Galamb utca 3 (#1, #4, #5), SegwayBP at Haris köz 2 (#2, #6) and E-Magine at Bécsi utca 8 (#3, #9). The EZRaider starts at Kinizsi utca 14 by the Great Market Hall, and the night Segway's start depends on the option.

Bring: a passport or ID card (several shops ask for it), flat shoes (no heels on the MonsteRoller) and a light bag (backpacks are not allowed on #6).

What costs extra: tips, food and drinks, the Ruszwurm or Castle Hill café stops and paid entries such as Matthias Church. Rain ponchos and winter gloves are included on most rides.

Weather: tours run in light rain with ponchos.

Planning the rest of the day? See the best things to do in Budapest.

faqs.q: How much does a Segway tour in Budapest cost?
faqs.a: From €35 for the 1-hour Express to €86 for the 3-hour Grand City Tour. The best value per hour is the 2-hour Buda and Pest ride at €54 (€26.80 an hour).

faqs.q: Do Segway tours in Budapest go up to Buda Castle?
faqs.a: Some do. The 2-hour Buda & Pest ride (#2), the Castle District tour (#4), the 3-hour Grand City tour (#6) and the night ride (#7) climb to Fisherman's Bastion and Matthias Church. The 90-minute (#1) and 1-hour (#5) rides stay in Pest.

faqs.q: Can kids do a Segway tour in Budapest?
faqs.a: From age 6 on #2, 7 on #6 and #7, 8 on #1, 9 on #5 and 10 on #4, usually with a 29–30 kg minimum weight. For younger children, the EZRaider (#8) takes kids from 3 in tandem with an adult.

faqs.q: Do I need a licence for an e-scooter in Budapest?
faqs.a: No. The wide-wheel MonsteRoller counts as an e-bike and uses cycle lanes. Drivers on the guided tour must be 14+, and bike or scooter experience is recommended.

faqs.q: Is there a weight limit on Segways?
faqs.a: Yes: 125 kg on the Castle District tour (#4), 129 kg on the Express (#5) and 140 kg on #2. The minimum is about 29–30 kg.

faqs.q: Segway or e-scooter: which should I pick?
faqs.a: A Segway is easier to learn and every tour starts with training. A MonsteRoller is faster and feels like a bike, so pick it if everyone in your group rides a bike confidently.

methodology: We compared 9 of Budapest's most popular Segway, wide-wheel e-scooter and EZRaider rides on the details that decide the booking: whether the route climbs Castle Hill, ride time and how much of it is training, price per hour, private or shared group, what is included and the age and weight limits. Prices are live from-prices for a normal date.
